certification.name: PyTorch Core: Practical ML & Neural Networks

concepts.name: Creating tensors
concepts.description: `torch.tensor(...)` creates a tensor from existing Python data, while factory functions such as `torch.zeros` and `torch.randn` create new tensor values.

concepts.name: Shape, dimensions, and element count
concepts.description: `tensor.shape` reports dimension sizes, `tensor.ndim` reports the number of dimensions, and `tensor.numel()` reports the total number of elements.

concepts.name: dtype, device, and `.to(...)`
concepts.description: A tensor has a `dtype` and a `device`, and `.to(...)` can move it to another device or convert its dtype.

concepts.name: Random seeds
concepts.description: `torch.manual_seed(seed)` sets the seed for generating random numbers on all devices for PyTorch random-number generators.

concepts.name: `reshape` and `view`
concepts.description: `reshape` changes tensor shape while preserving the number of elements and may return either a view or a copy.

concepts.name: `unsqueeze` and `squeeze`
concepts.description: `unsqueeze(dim)` inserts a size-1 dimension, while `squeeze(dim)` removes a size-1 dimension at the selected position.

concepts.name: `permute` and `transpose`
concepts.description: `permute(...)` reorders multiple dimensions, while `transpose(dim0, dim1)` swaps two dimensions.

concepts.name: `cat` vs `stack`
concepts.description: `torch.cat` joins tensors along an existing dimension, while `torch.stack` joins tensors along a newly created dimension.

concepts.name: Broadcasting
concepts.description: Broadcasting lets compatible tensor shapes participate in elementwise operations without explicitly copying values to the larger shape.

concepts.name: Reductions and `dim`
concepts.description: Reduction operations such as `sum` and `mean` reduce values along selected dimensions, and `keepdim=True` preserves reduced axes with size 1.

concepts.name: Matrix multiplication
concepts.description: `torch.matmul` and the `@` operator perform matrix multiplication with PyTorch broadcasting rules for batched dimensions.

concepts.name: Softmax and argmax
concepts.description: `softmax` converts scores along a chosen dimension into values that sum to 1, while `argmax` returns the index of the largest value.
